- Overestimate prices in bullish sentiment periods (sentiment > 0.67), especially after recent spikes; reduce forecast peak values.
- Underestimate prices in bearish sentiment (sentiment < 0.33), particularly when sentiment turns negative; adjust downward bias.
- Overshoot after sharp upward moves (e.g., >80) — cap forecast peaks at 10–15% below true peak in subsequent days.
- Mean-reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above recent 5-day average, reduce by 5–10% unless sentiment strongly bullish.
- Lagged overreaction: if forecast is >10% above true outcome 3–5 days prior, adjust downward by 5–8% for next period.
- Sentiment-driven horizon mismatch: if sentiment is strong but forecast is flat or declining, increase forecast slope slightly to match sentiment momentum.
- Avoid overconfidence in early forecast days (e.g., day 1–3) — reduce initial forecast by 2–5% if sentiment is weak or mixed.
